submission.justification:
Radiator-R2 at 4 cm thickness is recommended as it provides the best pion/kaon separation performance among viable candidates. 

Key findings:
- Radiator-R3, while offering the highest separation power (4.6σ at 3cm), fails the critical ageing requirement with 40% transparency loss, far exceeding the 10% maximum allowed. Since the radiator cannot be replaced during the 10-year run, R3 must be excluded.
- Radiator-R1 passes ageing (3% loss) but achieves only 2.892σ separation at its optimal thickness of 4 cm.
- Radiator-R2 passes ageing comfortably (6% loss) and delivers 3.849σ separation at 4 cm thickness, representing a 33% improvement over R1.

The 4 cm thickness was determined through systematic simulation across the allowed 1-6 cm range, finding that R2 performance peaks at 4 cm before degrading at greater thicknesses. This configuration meets all hard constraints while maximizing the primary goal of pion/kaon separation.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 at 4 cm provides 3.849σ separation, which is the best performance among candidates that pass all constraints. This is 33% better than R1 (2.892σ) and R3 is disqualified due to ageing failure.

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 is one of the three official candidates (R1, R2, R3).

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 shows 6% transparency loss in ageing tests, well below the 10% maximum threshold (R2_ageing_transparency_loss_percent = 6).
Recommended thickness of 4 cm falls within the specified 1-6 cm range.
